title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 70
paragraphs: Then Isagoras, as he was being worsted in his turn, contrived a plan against him: he called in Cleomenes the Lacedaemonian to help him, who had been his guest-friend since the siege of the sons of Peisistratus; moreover Cleomenes was accused of being intimate with Isagoras's wife. First, then, Cleomenes sent a herald to Athens demanding the expulsion of Cleisthenes and with him many other Athenians, calling them “the accursed.” This message he sent at Isagoras's prompting; for the Alcmaeonidae and their party were accused of the murder to which this referred, while he and his friends had had no part in it.
